clue.text: Fellow, covered in fur, made Spooner utter a prayer

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words, so the phrase is said his way

blocks.note: a fellow is a male, and one covered in fur is hairy; swap the opening sounds of the pair

explanation.surface: A furry man forces the stammering clergyman to say a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: MALE HAIRY with its first sounds exchanged becomes HAIL MARY.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hail Mary is the Catholic devotional addressed to the Virgin, beginning with the angel's greeting.

clue.text: One of us is taking on relationship type of studies

indicators.note: taking something on means taking it in, so the short word holds the other piece

blocks.note: each of us is a human being
taken as written
a tie is a bond or relationship

explanation.surface: A person takes up relationship-based courses of learning.
explanation.definitionFit: The humanities are academic disciplines such as history, literature and philosophy, as opposed to sciences.

clue.text: Popular fiction genre has us on tenterhooks

blocks.note: in means fashionable or popular
suspense is a genre of thriller writing

explanation.surface: Thrillers keep readers on the edge of their seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anxiously uncertain and waiting for an outcome is the idiom of being kept on tenterhooks.

clue.text: Chinese region producing rainwear with gold finish

blocks.note: a mac is a raincoat, short for mackintosh
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A Chinese area manufactures raincoats trimmed in gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Macau is a special administrative region on China's south coast, a former Portuguese territory famous for casinos.

clue.text: Driver mood is perturbed delivering mobile furniture

indicators.note: a perturbed thing is thrown into disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An upset van man is bringing round portable furnishings.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'is' reads as grammar joining driver to his mood, but its letters belong in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Room dividers are movable screens or shelving units used to partition a space, so they are portable fittings.

clue.text: Admitted fellow is inside and not thrown out

indicators.note: something that is inside another sits within it, so one piece goes into the other

blocks.note: admitted means allowed entry, let in
F is the standard abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A man who was let in stays put rather than being expelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kept rather than discarded or cut is retained in, the reverse of being removed or omitted.

clue.text: Delight receiving green car for promotion

indicators.note: one word receiving another takes it in, so the second goes inside the first

blocks.note: elation is great delight
an EV, an electric vehicle, is the green kind of car

explanation.surface: Joy at getting an eco-friendly company car with a step up the ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: EV, short for electric vehicle, is the standard green car; electric cars count as environmentally friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevation is a raising in rank, a move up to a higher position at work.

clue.text: Sums made by heartless solicitors

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter of the word is cut out

blocks.note: touts are people who solicit custom, such as ticket sellers

explanation.surface: Totals added up by lawyers who lack compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitors' suggests lawyers; here it is those who solicit, touts. Drop the central U.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot, or tot up, is to add figures together, so tots are additions or totals.

clue.text: Regularly uncovers disagreeable voters

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals means every other one is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A habit of exposing grumpy electors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disagreeable' looks like unpleasant, but means those who disagree.
explanation.definitionFit: In parliamentary divisions the noes are those who cast votes against the motion.

clue.text: Nasty scum I fight for vintage entertainment system

indicators.note: something nasty is twisted and spoilt, so these letters are bent out of shape

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Someone vows to fight horrid riff-raff in defence of an old gramophone.
explanation.definitionFit: A clockwork case playing a tune from pinned cylinders was an old-fashioned device for home amusement.

clue.text: Little Scottish creature removes article for close friend

indicators.note: the creature word takes something away from itself, so a letter is dropped

blocks.note: beastie is the Scots word for a small animal, as in Burns's poem To a Mouse
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A wee Scottish animal discards an item to make a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the A out of BEASTIE to leave BESTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bestie is modern slang for one's best friend, the companion one is nearest to.

clue.text: Doctor creating oral list of health problems!

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A GP giving a spoken rundown of ailments.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the jocular phrase for someone reeling off every ailment, punning on a recital played on an organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Humorously, a recital of one's organs is a long catalogue of bodily complaints told to anyone listening.

clue.text: Nurses on mad rotation means nobody sleeps

indicators.note: a rotation is a turning round, so the letters are turned about into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Hospital nurses on a frantic shift pattern mean no one gets any rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a translation: the Puccini aria's Italian title means 'none shall sleep'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous tenor aria from Turandot has an Italian title literally rendered as 'let no one sleep'.

clue.text: Petty officials not so important when bidding for bridge

definitions.text: not so important when bidding for bridge

blocks.note: petty means minor, small
suits is slang for executives or bureaucrats in business clothes

explanation.surface: Small-minded bureaucrats matter less at a card table.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, clubs and diamonds score less than hearts and spades, so they rank lower in the auction.

clue.text: Sort I employed to put words together

definitions.note: describes the person, one employed for this

blocks.note: a sort is a type or kind
in a crossword, I is the setter speaking

explanation.surface: The setter describes being hired to compose text.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort' is also a printer's word for a piece of type, which fits the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A typesetter arranges type or text for printing, a job of assembling letters into pages.

clue.text: Fool starts to turn white eating raw prawns

indicators.note: the starts of the following words are their opening letters, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the initial letters of these five words

explanation.surface: An idiot goes pale after eating uncooked shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: A twerp is a silly or annoying person, a mild insult much like idiot or nitwit.

clue.text: Guideline creates safe environment for a strike

indicators.note: an environment surrounds whatever is placed in it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe
taken as written
to ram is to strike hard

explanation.surface: A rule sets up a secure setting for industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter is safecracker's slang, hence a 'peterman'. A RAM goes after its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A parameter is a limit or boundary that defines how something should be done, a working rule.

clue.text: Sextet with talent shows prospect of making it

blocks.note: six in Roman numerals
a talent is an ability

explanation.surface: A six-piece band's skill suggests they could be a success.
explanation.definitionFit: Viability is the capacity of a plan or business to work and succeed, its chance of surviving.

clue.text: Relaxed performer’s backstage requirement making classic film

blocks.note: easy means relaxed, at ease
a rider is the list of demands a touring act puts in its contract, such as dressing-room food and drink

explanation.surface: A laid-back star's dressing-room demands make for a great movie.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1969 road movie with Peter Fonda and Dennis Hopper on motorbikes is a counterculture landmark of cinema.

clue.text: Central economic unit some say is indispensable

definitions.note: the answer completes the saying: no one is indispensable

indicators.note: the central part of a word is its middle, so only the innermost letters are kept

blocks.note: the two middle letters of this eight-letter word
one is a unit, a single thing

explanation.surface: Some claim a core economic unit cannot be done without.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the familiar saying 'no one is indispensable': the answer fills the blank in front of 'is indispensable'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that every person can be replaced, so nobody at all is essential.

clue.text: Steam celery, then turn it into an empty vessel

indicators.note: the cook is told to turn the ingredients into something else, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe: cook the celery, then transform it into an empty bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mary Celeste was the ship found drifting crewless in the Atlantic in 1872, the archetypal abandoned vessel.

clue.text: Material delivered in oily crates

indicators.note: the answer comes packed inside the following words, as goods inside a crate

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Stretchy fabric arrives in greasy packing boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: Lycra is the trade name of a stretchy synthetic fibre used in sportswear and swimwear.

clue.text: Cut up nails that are cheap

definitions.note: a snip is a noun, a bargain: something that is cheap

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means reading the word from bottom to top

blocks.note: pins are small nails

explanation.surface: Trim the bargain nails.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives the word for a cut, and a snip is also British for a bargain.
explanation.definitionFit: A snip is a small cut made with scissors, and informally an item sold surprisingly cheaply.

clue.text: Chopper used in evacuated annexed zone

indicators.note: emptying a word removes its contents, so only its outside letters are left

blocks.note: first and last letters
first and last letters

explanation.surface: A tool carried in a cleared, occupied area.
explanation.definitionFit: An adze is an axe-like tool with an arched blade at right angles to the handle, for shaping wood.

clue.text: Novel little song sounds bare in this state

indicators.note: sounds asks for what the words sound like when spoken, not how they are spelt

blocks.note: novel means new, and a little song is a ditty

explanation.surface: A fresh short song sounds stripped down in this condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being bare means being unclothed, and the condition of having no clothes on is nakedness.

clue.text: Ordinary artist, half cut, becomes shopkeeper

indicators.note: cutting a word in half keeps only one of its halves, here the back one

blocks.note: stock as an adjective means ordinary or standard, as in a stock reply
the second half of this six-letter word

explanation.surface: A run-of-the-mill painter, rather drunk, turns into a retailer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half cut' is British slang for tipsy, which steers the surface away from cutting the word in half.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockist is a retailer that keeps a particular product line in its store for sale.

clue.text: Go wrong filling pastry for French chap

indicators.note: a filling sits inside its pastry case, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a pie is a pastry dish
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: A failed pastry filling for a Frenchman's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Filling' looks like the contents of the pie, which is apt: the error literally fills the pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre is a common French given name, the equivalent of Peter, so a typical man from France.

clue.text: Daily ingestion of sulphur may keep skin looking healthy

indicators.note: ingesting something means taking it inside, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: a daily is a British term for a cleaner who comes in each day
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: Taking sulphur every day might keep your complexion fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' looks like an adverb about the ingestion; it is the noun for a household cleaner. S goes inside CLEANER after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleanser is a cosmetic wash or lotion that removes dirt and oil from the face.
